extracted.intended_audience: donors and prospective grantees (animal welfare organisations, researchers, and advocates)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and criteria used by the EA Animal Welfare Fund to find, evaluate, and prioritise grants aimed at reducing farmed and neglected animal suffering worldwide. Includes fund priorities, evaluation factors, and operational principles for applicants and donors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theory of change
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessing theory of change
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate how proposed activities are expected to lead to concrete welfare outcomes for animals (i.e., the causal pathway from activities to impact). The fund assesses applicants’ articulated mechanisms for change when selecting grants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counterfactual impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessing counterfactual impact
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimate what would have happened in the absence of the grant — i.e., the marginal benefit attributable to the funding. The fund explicitly considers counterfactuals when comparing opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost-effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessing cost-effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare expected animal welfare benefits per dollar spent. Grants are prioritised based on how much welfare improvement (scale-adjusted) they are likely to deliver for the budget requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Likelihood of success
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessing likelihood of success
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate feasibility and the probability that the proposed activities will achieve their intended outcomes. This informs whether an otherwise promising intervention is worth funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigorous evaluation / systematic review of proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: Every grant is backed by rigorous evaluation; every grant undergoes systematic review
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The fund conducts thorough assessments of project proposals using systematic review processes to identify and select the most effective interventions. This includes internal review and use of evidence to support decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track outcomes and continuous improvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Systematically evaluate impact and adapt grantmaking strategies
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The fund aims to track outcomes from grants, publish payout reports and strategy updates, and use learnings to continuously improve its grantmaking. Applicants should expect monitoring and reporting requirements; the fund updates strategy based on observed results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Global outreach and solicitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Actively solicit applications worldwide to ensure a diverse range of high-impact projects
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The fund proactively seeks proposals from organisations and individuals across regions to surface neglected, high-impact opportunities — especially in the Global South and for neglected species.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic collaboration / partnership
rubrics_metrics.description: Partner with leading animal welfare organisations, researchers, and advocates
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The fund values proposals and work that leverage collaboration with established actors to increase reach and effectiveness. Partnerships and coordination are considered positive signals for potential impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pooled resources / pooled fund model
rubrics_metrics.description: Operate as a pooled fund combining contributions to unlock opportunities larger than single donors could fund
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pooling allows the fund to support both smaller and larger-scale initiatives and to shape a curated portfolio. Applicants should design projects appropriate to pooled-fund scale and timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: Commitment to openness in resource allocation processes
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The fund publishes payout recommendations, reports, and strategy updates to ensure responsible stewardship. Applicants and donors can expect public reporting on grants and rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversified portfolio across species, regions, and intervention types
rubrics_metrics.description: Build a diversified portfolio across species, regions, and intervention types
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The fund intentionally spreads risk and impact across multiple species (including invertebrates and aquatic animals), geographic regions (including Global South), and intervention strategies (corporate campaigns, policy advocacy, R&D). Donors seeking funding for a single narrow target may prefer a different vehicle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for incremental welfare improvements
rubrics_metrics.description: Fund many interventions that reduce farmed animal suffering through positive but incremental changes
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include corporate welfare campaigns and cage-free transitions. The fund explicitly funds incremental improvements when they are cost-effective and scalable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for systemic interventions (policy advocacy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Also support systemic interventions such as policy advocacy
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The fund funds work aimed at system-level change (e.g., legal protections, policy shifts) alongside incremental interventions, evaluating these for counterfactual impact and feasibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority: Ending cage confinement globally
rubrics_metrics.description: One of six 3-year strategic priorities: ending cage confinement globally
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fund favours corporate campaigns and policy advocacy targeting regions where millions of hens remain caged with little welfare oversight (notably the Global South). Recent grants include cage-free training and policy work in multiple countries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority: Aquatic animal welfare
rubrics_metrics.description: One of six 3-year strategic priorities: aquatic animal welfare
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fund supports R&D and on-farm improvements for farmed shrimp and fish across Asia, Africa, and Latin America (e.g., humane chill-killing research).

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority: Humane slaughter as the default
rubrics_metrics.description: One of six 3-year strategic priorities: making humane slaughter the default
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funding focused on global corporate and producer outreach to end the most painful forms of slaughter (with emphasis on shrimp and other high-suffering supply chains).

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority: Protecting neglected species (invertebrates)
rubrics_metrics.description: One of six 3-year strategic priorities: protecting neglected species
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Act before invertebrate farming scales; fund early-stage work to prevent entrenched systems that would cause widespread suffering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority: Wild animal suffering research and pilots
rubrics_metrics.description: One of six 3-year strategic priorities: wild animal suffering
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support research and pilot interventions in urban and agricultural settings to identify cost-effective ways to reduce wild animal suffering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority: Building the Global South ecosystem
rubrics_metrics.description: One of six 3-year strategic priorities: building the Global South ecosystem
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide core funding and movement coordination for advocates in Asia, Africa, and Latin America to strengthen local capacity and enable regionally appropriate interventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fit for donor preferences (targeted vs pooled)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider whether donors prefer pooled, diversified funding or targeted earmarks
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The fund is designed to maximise overall impact via a curated pooled portfolio; donors who want funds directed to a single species, intervention, or region may prefer a more targeted vehicle.
